LobbySettings.description: Island Battles game_settings for a lobby create request. Choose at most one map: map_template_id or map. The map must be made for exactly the lobby's teams: player_amount equal to the team count, and castle team colours exactly 1 to that count, in team order, with 0 for neutral castles. Without a map the game starts on a generated map. turn_timeout_seconds sets how long each turn lasts, from 5 to 600 seconds, 30 when left out, or null for no limit. An invalid choice fails lobby creation with invalid_game_settings, and its detail names each invalid field, such as game_settings.map.castles[0].x.

When a turn's deadline passes before every player has completed it, each team with a player who hadn't loses, and the game ends.

channel.description: The lobby's watch channel, watch:island-battles:<lobby_id>, which receives WatchGenerationEvent after each turn and WatchGameEndedEvent after the last one.

lobby_round.description: The lobby round that the game plays. A lobby plays one game per round, and the /game/from-lobby/{lobby_id} routes serve its newest game: compare this with the lobby snapshot's lobby.round to tell whether the game is the one the lobby started last.

outcome.description: How the game ended. Absent while the game runs.

teams.description: The teams that play, with their lobby names and the display names their players had at the start.

turn_deadline_at.description: When this generation's turn times out, as in GenerationState. Null when turns have no time limit, and once the game has ended. Watchers never apply a deadline themselves.

LobbyBearer.description: Guest bearer credential issued by POST /lobby/v1/sessions. This is distinct from a Centrifugo connection JWT.

PlayerToken.description: A player token for the island-battles game, from POST /lobby/v1/player-tokens with game_key island-battles: a JWT signed with EdDSA that the game verifies with the lobby's public keys, GET /lobby/v1/jwks.json, without reading the lobby. It lasts at most 15 minutes, until its expires_at; get a new one before then, at about 80 % of its life, and once more when a request answers 401. The guest credential of POST /lobby/v1/sessions is refused here: a missing, expired or invalid token is 401.

SubmitToken.description: A submit token from a TurnDelivery, submit.token, which starts with ibst1. It authorizes POST /generation/commands for one player's turn of one generation of one game, until the turn's deadline plus 30 seconds, or 24 hours after the generation when turns have no time limit.

UploadToken.description: An upload token from POST /game/lobbies/{lobby_id}/bot-packages/upload-token, which starts with ibut1. It stands for its player in POST /game/lobbies/{lobby_id}/bot-packages and its complete, for that lobby only, for 15 minutes. Its payload, the base64url JSON between its two dots, names the lobby as lobby_id, which the command line reads.

info.description: Operations a player client calls during a started game. After every turn, each roster player's Centrifugo channel `player:{player_id}` receives a `GenerationEvent`, except after the turn that ends the game, which pushes a `GameEndedEvent` with the final generation and its outcome instead. Clients reconcile with the generation read after subscribing or reconnecting; HTTP state is authoritative, and its `outcome` is set once the game has ended. A turn times out at its `turn_deadline_at`; the server runs no timers, so a client waiting for other players calls `POST /game/from-lobby/{lobby_id}/deadline` about a second after it. `MapTemplate` is the map file format, which `POST /map/create` accepts. `LobbySettings` is the `game_settings` object of an Island Battles lobby create request; `GET /map/templates` lists the default maps it can choose. `GET /game/upgrades` lists what each castle upgrade level costs, and `GET /bots/defaults` the default bots that the backend plays. Before getting ready in a lobby, every member chooses their bot in their lobby member settings with the lobby's `setLobbyMemberSettings`: `{"bot": {"kind": "localhost"}}`, their own bot, whose turns their client relays, or `{"bot": {"kind": "default", "level": N}}`, a default bot level; `GenerationState.bot` reports it during the game. `Demo` is the demo file format, which `GET /game/from-lobby/{lobby_id}/demo` returns and the demo viewer at `/game/demo-viewer/` opens. People outside the roster watch a game with its lobby's join code (`POST /lobby/v1/watches`): the lobby's watch channel `watch:island-battles:{lobby_id}` receives a `WatchGenerationEvent` after every turn and a `WatchGameEndedEvent` after the last, in the same push as the players' events, and `GET /game/from-lobby/{lobby_id}/watch` and `/watch/demo` are their reads. `BotTurn` and `BotTurnResult` are the stateless bot contract: a bot gets a `BotTurn` each turn and answers with a `BotTurnResult`, which is sent as one completing batch. A localhost bot gets its turns as a `TurnDelivery` from `GET /game/from-lobby/{lobby_id}/turn-delivery`, which its player's client posts to it, and submits its answer itself with the delivery's one-turn submit token. Any member of a lobby can upload a bot package, the zip that the SDKs' `package` command builds, to the lobby: `POST /game/lobbies/{lobby_id}/bot-packages` presigns the upload, the zip goes straight to storage, and `POST /game/lobbies/{lobby_id}/bot-packages/{package_id}/complete` checks it. The command line uploads with an upload token from `POST /game/lobbies/{lobby_id}/bot-packages/upload-token` instead of a session.
info.title: Island Battles Player API

get.description: Lists the default bots in level order, each with its level, a name and a description of how it plays. Higher levels play better. The backend plays a default bot itself, with no client: it plays each turn as soon as the generation is created, so it never misses a turn's deadline. A game in which only default bots are left plays on by itself, and each game request continues it for a few seconds. The list is static and needs no authentication.
get.summary: List the default bots that the backend plays.

post.description: Requires a place on the game's frozen roster; the lobby is not consulted. The server runs no timers, so a turn times out when a request applies its deadline, GenerationState.turn_deadline_at. Every game request does that first, and a client that is waiting for other players calls this once about a second after the deadline. Before the deadline, and for a game that has ended or has no turn timeout, it changes nothing. After it, every team with a player who hasn't completed the turn loses, the game ends with reason turn_timeout, and among the other teams still standing the team with the most castles wins; equal counts, or no team left, are a draw. The open generation stays the final one, game.ended is pushed to every roster player, and later commands conflict (409) with problem type urn:island-battles:problem:game-ended. Calling it again is safe and ends the game once. Returns your current state, as GET /game/from-lobby/{lobby_id}/generation does. A lobby can play several games, one per round (lobby.round, raised by POST /lobby/v1/games/island-battles/lobbies/{lobby_id}/reopen once a game has ended); this route serves the lobby's newest game and its frozen roster, and an older game can't be reached once the next one starts.
post.summary: Apply the current turn's deadline for a roster player

get.description: Requires a place on the game's frozen roster; the lobby is not consulted. Returns the game as a demo file, the Demo schema, as an attachment named island-battles-game-<game_id>-generation-<n>.json, where n is the number of generations played. Any roster player can save a demo at any time: one saved during the game holds the generations played so far and a null outcome. Each frame's game log lines follow the rule of GET /game/from-lobby/{lobby_id}/logs when the demo is saved: while the game runs only your own team's lines, once it has ended every team's. The demo viewer at /game/demo-viewer/ opens the file without the lobby, a session or the game. The body is streamed, and a long game with full logs takes tens of megabytes, so it is packed with gzip (Content-Encoding: gzip) when Accept-Encoding allows it. The game is deleted 7 days after its last generation by default; then this returns 404. A lobby can play several games, one per round (lobby.round, raised by POST /lobby/v1/games/island-battles/lobbies/{lobby_id}/reopen once a game has ended); this route serves the lobby's newest game and its frozen roster, and an older game can't be reached once the next one starts.

Content-Disposition.description: attachment, with the demo's file name.

Content-Encoding.description: gzip when the request's Accept-Encoding allows it; absent otherwise.

get.summary: Save a lobby's game as a demo file for a roster player

get.description: Requires a place on the game's frozen roster. The game does not consult the lobby, so access continues after the lobby is deleted. Returns castle and soldier group IDs, which are never reassigned within a game, troop state, every castle's and soldier group's upgrade levels, recorded clashes with per-participant before/after counts, your turn completion flag, the turn's deadline, and the outcome once the game has ended. Like every game request, it first applies the turn's deadline once it has passed, which ends the game. A finished game stays readable until the game is deleted, 7 days after its last generation by default; then this returns 404. A lobby can play several games, one per round (lobby.round, raised by POST /lobby/v1/games/island-battles/lobbies/{lobby_id}/reopen once a game has ended); this route serves the lobby's newest game and its frozen roster, and an older game can't be reached once the next one starts.
get.summary: Read the current generation for a roster player

get.description: Requires a place on the game's frozen roster; the lobby is not consulted. Returns the game log lines that players' bots sent with their batches for the generation, grouped by player, each named by the display name they had at the start, never by ID. While the game runs you see only your own team's lines; once it has an outcome you see every team's. hidden_team_colors lists the teams you can't see yet, without saying whether they logged anything. A generation of another game returns 404. The lines are deleted with the game, 7 days after its last generation by default; then this returns 404. A lobby can play several games, one per round (lobby.round, raised by POST /lobby/v1/games/island-battles/lobbies/{lobby_id}/reopen once a game has ended); this route serves the lobby's newest game and its frozen roster, and an older game can't be reached once the next one starts.

get.description: Requires a place on the game's frozen roster; the lobby is not consulted. Returns the caller's turn of the current generation as a TurnDelivery: the BotTurn the server builds for their bot (the board, their team, the upgrade cost table, the memory their latest completed turn sent and the deadline), and how to submit the answer: submit.url, POST /generation/commands on the game's public URL, and submit.token, a submit token that submits exactly this player's turn of this generation. A game client relays it to the player's bot server, island-battles-bot serve, which answers 202 at once, plays the turn and submits its commands, logs and memory itself, with complete true and Authorization: Bearer <token>; the client submits nothing. Each call issues a new token for the same turn. Like every game request, it first applies the turn's deadline once it has passed. When the caller has nothing to play it returns 409: the game has ended (problem type urn:island-battles:problem:game-ended), their team has been eliminated, or they have already completed the turn. A lobby can play several games, one per round (lobby.round, raised by POST /lobby/v1/games/island-battles/lobbies/{lobby_id}/reopen once a game has ended); this route serves the lobby's newest game and its frozen roster, and an older game can't be reached once the next one starts.
get.summary: Read your turn as a delivery for your bot, with a one-turn submit token

get.description: For the people who watch the lobby with its join code (POST /lobby/v1/watches): a watcher the host hasn't kicked, an active member of the lobby, or a roster player. Returns the WatchState: the board, the teams, the turn's deadline and the outcome once the game has ended, without the player-only fields of GenerationState. The lobby's watch channel, WatchState.channel, receives WatchGenerationEvent after each turn and WatchGameEndedEvent after the last one, in the same push as the players' events; read this after subscribing or reconnecting. A watcher never plays and never delays a turn. Like the other game reads, it first applies the turn's deadline once it has passed. A kicked watcher gets 403. Anyone else, a lobby whose game hasn't started, and a lobby that was deleted get 404. A lobby can play several games, one per round (lobby.round, raised by POST /lobby/v1/games/island-battles/lobbies/{lobby_id}/reopen once a game has ended); this route serves the lobby's newest game and its frozen roster, and an older game can't be reached once the next one starts.
get.summary: Read the current generation of a lobby's game for a watcher

get.description: For the people who may read GET /game/from-lobby/{lobby_id}/watch. Returns the game so far as a demo file, the Demo schema, as GET /game/from-lobby/{lobby_id}/demo does, for scrubbing back through it. A watcher belongs to no team, so while the game runs no game log lines are included and every frame's hidden_team_colors names every team; once the game has ended every team's lines are. Packed with gzip when Accept-Encoding allows it. A lobby can play several games, one per round (lobby.round, raised by POST /lobby/v1/games/island-battles/lobbies/{lobby_id}/reopen once a game has ended); this route serves the lobby's newest game and its frozen roster, and an older game can't be reached once the next one starts.

get.description: Requires an active membership of the Island Battles lobby, in any phase, with your player token (PlayerToken); anyone else gets 404. Lists every package that a member uploaded and completed, newest first, with who uploaded it, its language, its entry or command and its size. A member has at most one. Packages are deleted 8 days after their upload, with their zips. A server without storage for packages answers 503.

post.description: Requires an active membership of the Island Battles lobby, in any phase, with your player token (PlayerToken) or an upload token for this lobby (Authorization: Bearer ibut1.…); anyone else gets 404, and an upload token for another lobby, or an expired one, 401. A bot package is the zip that the SDKs' package command builds: island-battles-bot package in Python, or the Go SDK's island-battles-package. A package belongs to the lobby, and anyone in it may upload one. This stores a pending package and returns its package_id and a presigned POST: send a multipart/form-data POST to upload.url with every field of upload.fields, unchanged, and the zip last, in a field named file. The zip goes straight to storage, never through this server, so it may be up to 250 MiB (262,144,000 bytes); the presigned POST refuses an empty or larger file, and expires after 15 minutes. Then call POST /game/lobbies/{lobby_id}/bot-packages/{package_id}/complete. file_name must end in .zip, or this is 422. A server without storage for packages answers 503.
post.summary: Start uploading a bot package to a lobby

post.description: Requires an active membership of the Island Battles lobby, in any phase, with your player token (PlayerToken); anyone else gets 404. Returns an upload token for you and this lobby, valid for 15 minutes, for a command line that doesn't hold your session: island-battles-bot upload --game-url <url> --token <token> dist/island-battles-bot.zip, or the Go SDK's island-battles-package upload with the same arguments. The two upload endpoints, POST /game/lobbies/{lobby_id}/bot-packages and its complete, accept it as Authorization: Bearer <token> in place of your player token; nothing else does. The command line reads the lobby from the token. A server without storage for packages answers 503.
post.summary: Get an upload token for uploading a bot package from the command line

delete.description: Requires an active membership of the Island Battles lobby, in any phase, with your player token (PlayerToken); anyone else gets 404. Deletes the package and its zip. Only the member who uploaded it can: anyone else gets 403. A package that the lobby doesn't have is 404. A server without storage for packages answers 503.
delete.summary: Delete your bot package from a lobby

post.description: Requires an active membership of the Island Battles lobby, in any phase, with your player token (PlayerToken) or an upload token for this lobby (Authorization: Bearer ibut1.…); anyone else gets 404, and an upload token for another lobby, or an expired one, 401. Only the member who started the upload can complete it; for anyone else the package is 404. It reads the zip's central directory and island-battles-bot.json with range requests, without downloading the zip, and checks that: the manifest is format 1, either python with python "3.14" and a module:function entry, or native with a command whose program is a file in the zip; the files come to at most 1 GiB (1,073,741,824 bytes) unpacked; and no path leaves the package (.., absolute paths or symbolic links). A package that fails a check is 422 with a detail that says what is wrong, and is deleted with its zip: start another upload. Before the zip is uploaded this is 409, and nothing changes. A valid package is the member's package in the lobby from then on, and every member sees it in GET /game/lobbies/{lobby_id}/bot-packages. A member has one package per lobby: completing a new one deletes their previous one. Completing it again returns it. A server without storage for packages answers 503.
post.summary: Check an uploaded bot package and add it to the lobby

get.description: Lists every upgrade type, sorted by type, with what its levels measure and, for each level from 1 to max_level, its effect and the soldiers a castle pays to reach it from the level below. Every castle starts at level 1. The table is static and needs no authentication. Castles and soldier groups carry their current levels, and upgrade_castle in POST /generation/commands buys the next one.
get.summary: List the castle upgrades, their levels and their costs.

post.description: Requires a player token of a player on the game's frozen roster (PlayerToken), or a submit token: Authorization: Bearer ibst1.… from GET /game/from-lobby/{lobby_id}/turn-delivery stands for its player for the batch of its game and generation only, and anything else (another game or generation, an expired or altered token, a player no longer on the roster) is 401. Either way the lobby is not consulted, and the rules below are the same. Players send send_soldier_group and upgrade_castle commands for castles their team owns; other command types are forbidden (403). upgrade_castle buys the next level of one upgrade type and pays that level's soldier_cost, listed by GET /game/upgrades, from the castle's soldiers. A castle may be upgraded several times in one turn, and each upgrade buys the next level. Every command is checked against the generation and every command already accepted this turn, including your own earlier batches, so an accepted command cannot fail when the turn runs. An invalid command rejects the whole batch, and nothing of it is stored. Malformed parameters are 422. Rejections that clients tell apart carry a problem type: a castle that is not in the generation is 422 urn:island-battles:problem:castle-not-found, an unknown upgrade_type is 422 urn:island-battles:problem:unknown-upgrade-type, a castle your team does not own is 403 urn:island-battles:problem:castle-not-owned, an upgrade past its type's max_level, counting this turn's upgrades, is 409 urn:island-battles:problem:upgrade-max-level, and soldiers or an upgrade cost beyond what the castle has left after this turn's reservations is 409 urn:island-battles:problem:insufficient-soldiers. A castle may spend all its soldiers. Complete defaults to true; an empty batch can complete a turn. The last frozen roster completion advances exactly once. The game ends after the turn that leaves one team with castles or soldier groups, a draw when the last teams are eliminated in the same turn, or after the turn that creates generation 300, where the team with the most castles wins. That turn's generation is the last, its state carries the outcome, and every later command conflicts (409) with problem type urn:island-battles:problem:game-ended. A turn also ends the game when its deadline, GenerationState.turn_deadline_at, passes before every roster player completed it: each team with a player who hadn't loses (outcome reason turn_timeout), the open generation stays the last, and a batch for it after the deadline conflicts with the same problem type. Retry the same request UUID and payload safely, also after the game ended; changed payloads and stale new requests conflict. A batch may also carry game log lines, which are stored in order with the generation and read with GET /game/from-lobby/{lobby_id}/logs. A player has at most 100 lines per generation, each of at most 500 characters; a batch over either limit is rejected whole (422) with problem type urn:island-battles:problem:game-log-limit. A batch may also carry the memory of the player's bot, any JSON object of at most 64 KiB as compact JSON. The batch with complete true saves it, replacing the player's previous memory, and an absent or null memory clears it; other batches ignore it. GenerationState.memory returns the memory sent with the player's latest completed turn, and the retry hash covers it. Larger memory is rejected whole (422) with problem type urn:island-battles:problem:bot-memory-too-large.
post.summary: Register an atomic player command batch and optionally complete the turn

post.description: Creates an authenticated Centrifugo connection token; it never creates or joins a lobby.

get.description: Lists every default map whose castle team colours are exactly 1 to player_amount, ordered by name. Choose one when creating an Island Battles lobby by passing its map_template_id in game_settings, with exactly team_count teams. Maps that fit no lobby are left out: those whose team colours skip a colour, and those made for fewer than 2 or more than 16 teams.
get.summary: List the default maps a lobby can start on.
